comparison_cases.name: Sanitized Network Flow (Good Counterpart)

latte.failure_reason: Ungrounded LLM suffers from 'Sink Trap' sensory bias: seeing 'execl' + 'recv' triggers automatic vulnerability prediction, ignoring the sanitizer check.

firmgraph.success_reason: GraphRAG queries Neo4j for pattern 'recv -> is_valid_alphanumeric -> execl'. Finds matching safe counter-pattern from training set; LLM prompt is grounded with sanitizer proof.

comparison_cases.name: Multi-Hop Pointer Aliasing & Intermediate Wrappers

latte.failure_reason: Context window dilution across multi-function call chain causes ungrounded LLM to lose pointer alias tracking (buffer -> dst -> msg -> alias -> fmt).

firmgraph.success_reason: Neo4j Call Graph performs topological path traversal: (read_input)-[:CALLS]->(wrap_log)-[:CALLS]->(print_msg). Injects exact call chain and parameter indices directly into prompt.

comparison_cases.name: Recurring Zero-Day Taint Pattern Across Firmware

latte.failure_reason: LATTE evaluates in complete isolation with zero historical memory. Cannot determine if this pattern has occurred in other firmware, resulting in low triage prioritization.

firmgraph.success_reason: Matches VulnPattern 'pattern::CWE-190::t::fscanf' with occurrence_count=159 in Neo4j. Multi-factor triage (0.5×LLM + 0.3×KG + 0.2×CWE) ranks this critical recurring flaw at the top.
